reflex-dev/xy
items.brief: 13,544 weekly downloads, up 11.5% in a day and 200% since 4 August, while stars moved 0.5%. Seventh straight appearance, and the gap between installing it and bookmarking it has never once closed.
items.description: A charting library for Python, from the team behind the Reflex web framework. It renders interactive charts directly from Python objects, so the analysis and the chart live in the same place instead of the data being handed to a JavaScript layer to draw. It ships on PyPI, and that is what makes the adoption measurable: a download is someone installing it into a project, a star is someone bookmarking it, and those two numbers have been moving in opposite directions here for two weeks.

items.name: TheRealYT/git-knife
items.brief: 291 stars, up 12.3%, with 165 HackerNews points and 101 comments. Open issues up 33.3% on the same day: the people who found it are using it hard enough to file bugs.
items.description: A desktop GUI for editing git commit metadata — the message, the author, and both the author and the committer dates. Existing git interfaces reword and reorder commits well but treat dates as fixed, and the tools that can rewrite them, git-filter-repo and commit-tree, have no interface at all. git-knife covers that gap by shelling out to the system git and rebuilding each commit from its original tree, so file contents are provably never altered.

items.name: antigma.ai
items.brief: Forks up 30.8% against stars up 12.7% in a day — 50 forks on 1,652 stars. Pushed the same day, and HackerNews has gone quiet at 1.8%, so the growth is running without a thread behind it.
items.description: Antigma, a terminal harness for running AI coding agents, published as the repository AntigmaLabs/ante. The agent loop, the tool calls and the sandbox ship in a single binary rather than being assembled from separate services, so the whole run happens on one machine and can be inspected afterwards. For a tool of this kind the fork count is the number that carries information: forking means taking the code away to change it, which is a different act from starring it.

still_moving.description: An inference engine written in C that runs the MiniMax H3 language model on Apple hardware, from Salvatore Sanfilippo, who wrote Redis. still_moving.name: palamim/starboard
still_moving.brief: Second appearance and every number moved the same direction again — stars 3.1%, forks 3.6%, open issues 20%. Modest, consistent, and pushed today rather than abandoned after the thread. On a 156-star repo these are a handful of people, but they are the same handful coming back, which at this size is all the evidence available.
still_moving.description: A terminal for macOS that lives permanently beside the Dock instead of appearing on a hotkey. The distinction is deliberate: a drop-down terminal is somewhere you visit, a docked one is somewhere you glance at, and the author is betting that glanceable changes how it gets used.

still_moving.name: MakazhanAlpamys/Soup
still_moving.brief: 68 open issues against 430 stars — a 16% ratio, roughly five times what a healthy young repo shows, and forks up 5.5% against 3% star growth. Both point the same way: the people arriving are running it and hitting walls, not bookmarking it. For a tool claiming to fine-tune an 8-billion-parameter model on ordinary hardware, hitting walls is exactly what you would expect and exactly what makes the claim testable. HackerNews has gone quiet at 0.7%, so this is now growing without a thread pushing it.
still_moving.description: Fine-tunes large language models from a single configuration file, streaming layers so an 8-billion-parameter model fits on ordinary hardware.

still_moving.name: t8y2/dbx
still_moving.brief: Third appearance. 13,242 stars with 1,344 forks — one fork per ten stars, where most repos manage one in fifty — and the ratio has held for a week rather than spiking and fading. Homebrew installs are the number to watch: a package-manager install puts it on a machine.
still_moving.description: A 20 MB cross-platform desktop client for querying more than 70 kinds of database from one window.

still_moving.name: leonickson1/Swiftlet
still_moving.brief: Third day, and the story is that it has stopped being a story. Stars up 2.1% and forks 2.4% — matched, modest, and a long way from the 13.2% fork surge two days ago. Open issues actually fell 25%, meaning the maintainer is clearing them faster than new ones arrive. That is a healthy repo and no longer a rising one, which is worth saying plainly rather than dressing up.
still_moving.description: A lightweight Swift web framework for building server-side applications.

still_moving.name: bobdahacker.com
still_moving.brief: A security researcher's site, on Lobsters with comments up 3.8% and points up 2.5%, alongside a 1.3% move in its traffic rank. Small numbers in every direction. It is here because three independent collectors saw it on the same day, which is the bar this list sets — but nothing about the magnitude says anything is happening yet.
still_moving.description: The site of a security researcher who publishes findings from breaking into consumer products and services.

still_moving.name: runtimewire.com
still_moving.brief: Worth a line for what it is rather than how it moved: a startup-intelligence service tracking AI funding rounds, which is a direct competitor to what this project is building. Pricing tiers up 33.3% means it added a plan — the monetisation signal the guide calls a binary riser trigger. On the HackerNews front page with 22 comments.
still_moving.description: A startup-intelligence service tracking funding rounds and company activity in AI.

still_moving.name: xoreaxeaxeax/asm-hall-of-shame
still_moving.brief: Stars up 38.4% in a day, forks up 12% and open issues up 20%, with GitHub, HackerNews and Lobsters all seeing it at once — three independent collectors and the widest star jump on today's list. Lobsters points more than doubled, up 108.8%, which for that community's size means it landed with almost everyone who saw it. A catalogue of the worst instructions in CPU history is the kind of thing that either gets ignored or gets contributed to, and 5 forks on 567 stars this early leans towards the second.
still_moving.description: A catalogue of the worst-performing machine instructions across CPU designs, collected by a well-known reverse engineer.

still_moving.name: jj-vcs/jj
still_moving.brief: Second appearance. Jujutsu at 30,887 stars is long past discovery, so what is being tracked is not whether it grows but whether Git users actually switch — and Homebrew installs are the only honest measure of that. Forks and issues barely moved today; the entry earns its place through three unrelated collectors agreeing, not through any single number.
still_moving.description: Jujutsu, a version-control system that works with existing Git repositories but replaces Git's commands with a simpler model.
